name: LoongServe (elastic sequence parallelism for long-context LLM serving)
notable_features: AN ARTIFACT-EVALUATION SUBMISSION, NOT A PRODUCT. This is the single most useful thing about the record. The repository's entire README is three lines pointing at an artifact-evaluation folder, and the AE guide is written for reviewers: log into the AUTHORS' cluster via a jump server, activate the environment, reserve compute nodes. That is an unusually candid signal about who the intended user is - the Artifact Evaluation committee, not operators

The technical contribution is ELASTIC SEQUENCE PARALLELISM for long-context serving: splitting prefill and decode across a variable number of GPUs as sequence length and load change, which is the part tensor parallelism cannot flex. Elastic matters because long-context requests have wildly different costs

The AE guide scripts the comparison against the field's canonical baselines explicitly: vLLM, LightLLM with SplitFuse, DeepSpeed-MII with Dynamic SplitFuse, and DistServe with prefill-decode disaggregation, each across ShareGPT, LEval, LV-Eval and a Mixed workload. That makes it a better map of the disaggregation design space than any single result would be

IT SHIPS A MODIFIED NCCL. The repository contains an 'rnccl' directory alongside 'longserve_cuda_kernels', which is the practical blocker: reproducing this requires building a custom collective-communication library, not just pip-installing a package
Apache-2.0, created 2024-08-21, last push 2024-11-11, 137 stars, 16 forks, 5 open issues, no GitHub releases
hardware_caveats: HARDWARE REUSE BARRIER, AND IT IS THE BINDING ONE. The system requires custom CUDA kernels (longserve_cuda_kernels) AND a modified NCCL (rnccl), plus multi-node launch (run_multi_nodes.sh). This is not a pip install. You are building a communication stack, which means the artifact only reproduces for people willing to do cluster work

THE DOCUMENTED PATH ASSUMES THE AUTHORS' CLUSTER. The artifact-evaluation guide's primary instructions are to log in via a jump server and reserve nodes on hardware the team controls, with non-AE-reviewer instructions relegated to a secondary section. Even a diligent outsider is reproducing on unfamiliar infrastructure

DORMANT. Last push 2024-11-11, roughly two years before this record's date of 2026-10-04, with 5 open issues and no releases. Not archived, so not formally deprecated - the same dormant-not-abandoned ambiguity as [[niche-routellm]] - but with no commits for two years it is not being maintained

I PUBLISH NO INDEPENDENT THROUGHPUT NUMBER HERE. The paper reports results (the AE guide refers to Figures 2, 3, 10, 11, 13, 14) but I have not extracted or independently verified any figure, and the repo publishes no standalone benchmark table. Any LoongServe speedup figure you see attributed to this record is paper-reported, not verified here
SMALL AND NARROW: 137 stars, 16 forks. This is a research artifact from a paper team, not a project with a user community
CUDA ONLY, no ROCm, no CPU, no Metal. The custom kernels and modified NCCL make portability close to zero

BUILT ON TOP OF A MOVING TARGET. Baseline comparisons were run against vLLM, LightLLM and DeepSpeed-MII as they existed in 2024. DeepSpeed-MII is now recorded as deprecated ([[niche-deepspeed-mii]]) and LightLLM is not a project most people deploy today ([[niche-lightllm]]), so the comparison set has aged badly even though the ideas have not
best_for: Studying elastic sequence parallelism as a technique - the code and the AE comparison matrix against DistServe, SplitFuse and vLLM make this the most useful artefact in this corner of the field
Reading how prefill-decode disaggregation was approached in 2024, alongside [[distserve]] and [[semi-pd]], which are the two records already in the repo
A research group willing to build custom CUDA and NCCL code and reproduce on their own multi-node cluster
Anyone surveying the disaggregation design space, since the AE guide is effectively a survey with runnable scripts
avoid_for: Production deployment of any kind. This is an artifact-evaluation submission and the documentation says so
Anyone who does not have multi-node GPU infrastructure and a willingness to build a modified NCCL
Expecting current model support, current kernels, or community maintenance - there have been no commits since 2024-11-11
Teams that need a vLLM-class serving system with support behind it - the ideas migrated into production stacks, the repo did not
notes: One of the paper-code releases people in disaggregated serving actually read, recorded for its artifact-evaluation guide rather than its performance: the scripted baseline matrix against DistServe, SplitFuse and vLLM across ShareGPT/LEval/LV-Eval is the most compact map of the 2024 disaggregation design space in this repo. The honest negatives dominate the positives: dormant since 2024-11-11, requires custom CUDA kernels plus a modified NCCL, and its primary documented reproduction path targets the authors' own cluster. Notably the baseline set has aged - DeepSpeed-MII is now itself a deprecated record. NO INDEPENDENT THROUGHPUT VERIFIED - the paper's figures are not extracted here and any number attributed to this record is paper-reported. Read together with [[distserve]] and [[semi-pd]] for the same problem space.
